evals.prompt: Install only the native Video Codec SDK and run an H.264 encode and decode smoke test.
evals.expected_output: Native-only setup verified with the official native encoder and decoder.
assertions: Selects only the native SDK and does not install PyNvVideoCodec
Inspects the Jetson release and reuses each compatible installed native prerequisite without reinstalling it

For each absent or invalid required APT package, inspects the exact candidate and origin, runs the apt-get -s simulation, and applies the identical reviewed package spec with standard APT commands directly
After any APT mutation, runs dpkg --audit and stops unless it exits zero with empty output
Uses package-owned AppEncCuda followed by package-owned AppDec and reports ready only after the decoder produces one frame from the fresh bitstream

evals.prompt: Install only PyNvVideoCodec in a new isolated Python environment and run an H.264 encode and decode smoke test.
evals.expected_output: Python-only setup verified with wheel-owned encoder and decoder samples.
assertions: Selects only PyNvVideoCodec and does not install the native SDK developer package
Uses the absent conventional smoke path when no alternative is supplied, creates it with standard venv and pip commands, then reports and uses its exact interpreter
Inspects the installed distribution and loaded module through that exact interpreter and keeps it selected throughout verification
Uses the wheel-owned encoder followed by a wheel-owned independent decoder and reports ready only after their one-frame markers and fresh bitstream pass

evals.prompt: PyNvVideoCodec is already installed. Reuse it and run an H.264 encode and decode smoke test.
evals.expected_output: The existing validated Python environment is reused without reinstallation and passes the smoke test.
assertions: Uses an exact supplied or current-conversation interpreter, otherwise checks only the conventional smoke path instead of scanning for environments
Does not reinstall packages or create another environment when the existing one is valid
Uses the wheel-owned encoder followed by an independent decoder before reporting ready

evals.prompt: Is my environment ready to run video SDK work right now? Probe the target and report readiness. (Report-only.)
evals.expected_output: A clarification asking whether to inspect native Video Codec SDK, PyNvVideoCodec, or both, with no target probe or action before the user chooses.
assertions: Treats the bare phrase video SDK as ambiguous even though the request is report-only
Asks whether the user wants native Video Codec SDK, PyNvVideoCodec, or both
Stops before target inspection, probing, planning, installation, building, or codec operations

evals.prompt: The official video sample passed in device-memory mode. Confirm that its frames can be shared zero-copy with another pipeline stage.
evals.expected_output: A readiness-only result that does not promote device-memory sample success to an external sharing or synchronization claim.
assertions: Separates the exact sample readiness result from buffer-interoperability evidence
Does not claim DMA-BUF, NvSciBuf, CUDA IPC, zero copy, or a synchronization primitive
Requires an authenticated interoperability test of the actual downstream stage that proves the sharing handle, format and layout, ownership and lifetime, signal and wait behavior, and safe reuse
